title: Lead Analyst, Financial Crimes
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Chime's Financial Crimes team protects millions of members from money laundering, fraud, and the organized networks that target consumer financial platforms. We work in a bank-partner model: we run detection and investigation, and we escalate unusual activity to our bank partners, who hold the filing obligation. That means our written work product is read by outside parties, and the quality bar is correspondingly high.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You will set the standard for how financial crime work is done here rather than working a queue — defining what good looks like, raising the ceiling for the analysts you lead, and owning the hardest problems on the team end to end.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Operate with minimal direction on problems that arrive ambiguous, and you define the approach rather than waiting for one.
  • Set the quality standard others calibrate to with defensible judgement calls.
  • Move work across team boundaries without formal authority, and you are trusted to represent Financial Crimes to partners outside the function.
  • Raise the ceiling of the people around you — through calibration, coaching, documentation, and the examples you set in your own casework.
  • Improve the system, not just the case. Every hard investigation should leave behind something reusable: a control, a procedure, a detection change, or a documented typology.
  • What you will own:
    • Vendor Management. You will lead, and support, a team of analysts.
    • Vendor team quality. You sample operations work, run calibration with partners, keep apprised of quality assurance trends, and hold quality and productivity expectations where they belong.
    • Risk trend analysis. You understand AML and Fraud risks well enough to follow the pattern of unusual activity across accounts, devices, funding sources, counterparties, and behavioral patterns, and you can show the shape of a network in a way a non-investigator understands.
    • Typology development. You document new and evolving schemes, make them teachable to the wider team, identify if opportunities in coverage are needed, and own the creation of coverage with partners as appropriate.
    • Operational rollout of new coverage. When a new typology or scenario goes live, you design how it will be worked — routing, procedure, evidence standard, and quality checks — before the first alert lands.
    • Procedures and documentation. You own the SOPs for your area and keep them in a state where a third party could read them cold and understand what we do and why.
    • Audit and exam readiness. You prepare the operational side for internal audit, independent testing, and bank partner reviews, and you own remediation of findings assigned to operations through to closure.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • 7+ years in financial crime, fraud, or risk investigations at a bank, fintech, payments company, or comparable regulated environment.
  • Working command of BSA, the USA PATRIOT Act, OFAC requirements, and unusual/suspicious activity reporting standards — enough to explain not just the rule but why it exists.
  • Deep experience across the transaction monitoring alert lifecycle at real volume, including the operational tradeoffs that come with it.
  • Real typology depth across both money laundering and fraud — mule and money movement networks, first-party fraud, synthetic and stolen identity, scams and social engineering, elder financial exploitation, etc.
  • Hands-on involvement in scenario tuning or threshold work alongside data or risk partners, with an understanding of what changing a threshold actually costs.
  • Experience overseeing vendor or outsourced investigation teams.
  • Judgment under volume. You can distinguish the case that deserves forty hours from the one that deserves forty minutes.  
  • Comfort with sustained ambiguity. You will spend real time on hypotheses that do not pan out, and you need the judgment to know when to stop.
  • Advanced SQL, and fluency with graph or link analysis tooling for mapping relationships at scale.
  • CAMS, CFE, or equivalent certification preferred.

descriptionHtml:
About the Role

The Sr. Associate, Compliance Advisory partners with Complaints, Product, Operations, and other business teams to provide compliance guidance as a second line of defense. The role supports consumer complaint oversight, new and existing product operations advisory, agent readiness, member- and agent-facing communications, and process improvement while identifying consumer and regulatory risks and helping drive issues through remediation and implementation.

In this role, you can expect to

Complaints Management

  • Advise the first line of defense on complaint-management requirements, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices.
  • Review complaint-handling processes, procedures, controls, and documentation; identify gaps and recommend remediation, maintaining ownership of the issue lifecycle from informing the business of identified gaps and recommendations through completed remediation and implementation.
  • Recommend and implement process improvements that balance regulatory requirements with innovative, member-friendly solutions.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of and apply consumer financial regulations—including Regulations Z, E, and DD, UDAAP, NACHA, VISA Operating Standards, and applicable state requirements—through compliance advisory work and day-to-day responsibilities.
  • Support operational teams in investigating and resolving consumer complaints while analyzing trends and potential member impact.
  • Perform oversight and monitoring to promote timely, accurate, and appropriate complaint resolution.
  • Develop and refine complaint procedures, guidance, training materials, and educational resources.
  • Assist with responses to sensitive and regulatory complaints and inquiries.
  • Ensure complaint-related work, processes, procedures, and guidance align with all applicable requirements of the Complaints Policy.
  • Support regulatory, bank partner, and internal audit readiness by collecting, organizing, and validating requested documentation and helping ensure complaint processes and records are complete and current.
  • Review complaint dashboards and complaint trends to identify emerging risks, recurring issues, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Present compliance findings, complaint trends, risk assessments, recommendations, training, and process updates to business partners and relevant business stakeholders when needed.
  • Prepare executive-level reports and presentations on compliance findings data, trends, risks, and recommendations.

Compliance Advisory

  • Provide compliance advisory support for operations supporting new products and changes to existing products, including identifying compliance considerations and helping teams address related risks and requirements.
  • Translate complex compliance requirements and data-driven insights into clear, practical, and actionable guidance for business partners and member-facing teams.
  • Support agent readiness for new products and changes to existing products by partnering on agent-facing communications, member-facing communications, help center articles, training, and other agent-ready content.
  • Partner with Compliance, Legal, Quality Control, Quality Assurance, bank partners, and business teams to mitigate compliance risk.
  • Demonstrate strong proficiency in AI tooling and proactively identify responsible AI-enabled tools and workflows that help the Compliance Advisory team work more efficiently and effectively.
  • Use AI tooling to accelerate data analysis, complaint-trend identification, monitoring, oversight, research, documentation, reporting, and preparation of business-partner guidance while maintaining appropriate human review and compliance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Leverage AI-enabled insights to help business partners make faster, better-informed decisions and improve outcomes for members.
  • Support quality assurance and quality control business partners as a second line of defense by helping ensure the program is regulatory sound, appropriately designed, and operating effectively for its intended purpose.
  • Serve as a knowledgeable Compliance presence in meetings with bank partners and business partners by contributing to discussions, answering questions, and identifying compliance considerations.

Core Competencies

  • Consumer complaints and complaint-program management and oversight.
  • Regulatory knowledge, including the ability to interpret applicable regulations and translate them into practical, risk-based guidance for products, processes, and member experiences.
  • Risk identification, escalation, and remediation.
  • Executive and business-partner communication and presentation skills.
  • Data analysis, automation, and practical application of AI tools.
  • Cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management.
  • Process documentation, monitoring, training, and continuous improvement.
  • Independent execution and resourcefulness, including taking end-to-end ownership.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • 5+ years of compliance experience in fintech, banking, or financial services, including meaningful work supporting consumer financial products and a track record of operating with a high degree of independence
  • Direct, hands-on experience with deposit accounts and credit products
  • Hands-on experience with consumer complaints and complaint-program management and oversight
  • Strong regulatory knowledge, with the ability to interpret applicable regulations and translate them into practical, risk-based guidance for products, processes, and member experiences
  • A sharp instinct for risk identification, escalation, and remediation — and the persistence to see issues through to closure

  • Experience with process documentation, monitoring, training, and continuous improvement

title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Enablement
descriptionHtml:
About the role

As a Senior Software Engineer on the AI Enablement team, you will build the internal platforms, primitives, and guardrails that make AI a trusted co-pilot for employees across Chime.

You’ll work on systems like Archimedes, Bosun, and easyRAG that power internal AI assistants, developer workflows, and retrieval-backed applications. These platforms make it easier for teams across the company to build, adopt, and scale LLM-powered tools safely and effectively.

This team defines Chime’s golden paths for AI: opinionated but flexible patterns that help teams move quickly while maintaining safety, reliability, cost control, and governance. In this role, you’ll help turn emerging AI capabilities into durable, reusable platform features that can be adopted across the company.

You’ll partner closely with Platform Engineering, Security, Risk, Legal, and product teams to build scalable, well-governed systems that support internal AI use cases from early prototyping through production adoption.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Build and evolve internal AI platforms such as Archimedes, Bosun, and easyRAG, enabling teams to develop and scale LLM-powered applications and workflows
  • Design and implement reusable platform capabilities such as APIs, SDKs, templates, and shared services that make it easier to build safe, high-quality AI-powered tools
  • Prototype and productionize new AI capabilities, identifying high-leverage use cases and turning successful patterns into durable platform features
  • Define and improve Chime’s golden path patterns for LLM usage, balancing developer velocity with safety, reliability, and cost efficiency
  • Develop systems that let teams launch AI-powered assistants and workflows in a standardized, observable, and governed way
  • Establish evaluation, observability, and cost-management practices across AI systems, including quality, latency, safety, and spend

title: Lead Data Scientist, Credit Risk
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Credit Risk Data Scientist who is data-driven, has strong analytical and technical skills, and operates with a high degree of ownership. In this role, you will lead the credit strategy that lets Chime lend to people before they have a relationship with us — starting with Instant Loans for new members (top of funnel) and expanding to future unsecured credit products such as credit cards. You'll develop risk policies and strategies to manage credit risk throughout the member lifecycle, and you'll work as a trusted cross-functional partner with product, growth, data engineering, machine learning, and analytics teams, interacting with business stakeholders across many departments.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Own credit strategy for new-to-Chime applicants across the member lifecycle, starting with Instant Loans for prospects (top of funnel) and extending to future unsecured products such as credit cards and/or lines of credit
  • Develop and evolve channel-specific credit policies (pre-approval / prescreen, direct mail, open application, referrals, and affiliates) that support growth while balancing risk, unit economics, and member experience
  • Design and continuously iterate acquisition, loan amount / line assignment, pricing, line management, repayment, and collections strategies
  • Leverage credit bureau (e.g., Experian), alternative, and internal Chime data to underwrite applicants with no prior Chime relationship; build credit models and policies hands-on and in partnership with our DSML team
  • Lead test-and-learn: design and read out champion/challenger tests and controlled ramps, and quantify trade-offs among approvals, losses, direct deposit conversion, and lifetime value
  • Partner with Finance and Strategy to size new channels and forecast approval funnels, vintage losses, and unit economics; set launch criteria, guardrails, and expansion triggers
  • Collaborate with data teams to build data infrastructure and early-read monitoring and dashboards (first payment default, delinquency, vintage and roll rates) that help senior management understand credit risk trends and exposures
  • Work with cross-functional teams including DSML, Product, Design, Engineering, and Decision Platform to test and implement risk models and strategies in production, including accurate adverse action reasons
  • Partner with Compliance, Legal, Fair Lending, Model Risk Management, Fraud, and our bank partners to document, approve, and govern credit policies
  • Mentor and work collaboratively with other credit risk data scientists to develop strategies, share knowledge, and raise the team's analytical bar

To thrive in this role, you have

  • A Master's degree (required) in Statistics, Economics, Engineering, Math, Finance, Computer Science, or another quantitative discipline; a PhD is a plus
  • 7+ years of analytical or data science experience in Financial Services, preferably at a FinTech company
  • 4+ years of experience building and managing risk for unsecured credit products such as installment loans, lines of credit, or credit cards; acquisition / underwriting experience strongly preferred
  • Hands-on experience with credit bureau data and prescreen, pre-approval, or direct mail credit programs
  • Experience with credit furnishing, bankruptcies, delinquency, and write-off policies, and working knowledge of consumer lending regulation (FCRA, ECOA / Reg B, fair lending, adverse action)
  • Excellent SQL and Python skills, advanced Microsoft Excel skills, and experience working in Looker or a similar business intelligence tool
  • A strong grounding in statistics and machine learning for credit, including scorecards / gradient-boosted models, swap-set analysis, vintage analysis, and experiment design
  • Hands-on, detail-oriented leader with exceptional communication skills who can explain a trade-off to executives and defend the math behind it
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, complex environment and meet ambitious deadlines while ensuring flawless completion
  • A strong passion for Chime's mission and solving challenging analytical problems for the business
  • Nice to have: subprime or near-prime lending, affiliate or marketplace lending, credit card line management, or cash-flow / alternative-data underwriting experience

title: Sr. Growth Product Marketing Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

We're hiring a Sr. Growth Marketing Manager to own and drive measurable growth outcomes across Chime Enterprise's B2B2C funnel — the path that turns eligible employees at our employer partners into enrolled, funded, and engaged Chime members.

Chime Enterprise is Chime's B2B business, with a vision to be the premier HR benefits platform dedicated to holistic financial wellness. Our flagship product, Chime Workplace, gives employers an all-in-one financial wellness suite at no cost — spanning capital management (including MyPay at Work), capital growth, credit building, and rewards and loyalty (Salt). Sales and Customer Success win and onboard employer partners; once a partner is live, we gain access to their workforce — their eligible employees. Converting those eligible employees into Chime members is the challenge this role owns, and mastering it unlocks one of the most powerful and defensible distribution channels at Chime.

This role is embedded directly within the cross-functional Chime Enterprise growth effort and operates as the growth owner, not just a marketing advisor. You'll sit at the intersection of growth strategy, experimentation, performance analysis, and product marketing craft: identifying opportunities, prioritizing and running experiments, and driving metric movement against clear goals. While the role retains core product marketing strengths — research, positioning, and messaging — it goes further by owning results and tradeoffs.

In this role, you can expect to

Growth Ownership & Strategy

  • Own end-to-end growth strategy and outcomes for Chime Enterprise's employee-side funnel, from opportunity sizing through roadmap delivery against quarterly and annual goals.
  • Serve as the embedded growth lead for Enterprise, co-owning planning with Enterprise Product, Engineering, and Analytics and with Growth Marketing's channel teams.
  • Build a repeatable model for converting eligible employees into members that scales across partners rather than being rebuilt deal by deal.

Funnel & Experimentation

  • Drive performance across the B2B2C funnel — worksite awareness, enrollment, funding, direct deposit, and early retention — with deep ownership of employer landing pages, eligibility flows, and in-product onboarding.
  • Own the Enterprise experimentation roadmap, designing reads that hold up at partner-sized cohorts and deciding what to scale, iterate, or sunset.
  • Lead creative and messaging execution for experiments and launches across paid, lifecycle, and owned surfaces.

Offers & Qualified Acquisition

  • Own incentives, promotions, and offers that drive qualified acquisition of primary banking relationships — balancing cost per enrollment, activation quality, and long-term value, within partner agreement and compliance guardrails.
  • Partner with Lifecycle to connect enrollment, onboarding, and retention into one journey.

GTM & Measurement

  • Lead GTM for employer launches, building the playbooks, campaign kits, and reporting that Sales, Customer Success, and GTM/Ops reuse at every go-live.
  • Track pacing against goals and translate results into clear briefs and recommendations for Enterprise and Growth Marketing leadership.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • 8+ years of experience in growth marketing, product marketing, performance marketing, or a related role (level dependent).
  • Proven experience driving measurable growth through experimentation and optimization, including owning a funnel metric end to end.
  • Experience marketing to end users through a partner, employer, or channel relationship — B2B2C, workplace or benefits marketing, marketplace, or embedded distribution — and comfort operating when you don't fully control the audience or the channel.
  • Strong analytical skills; ability to define success metrics, track performance, extract insights, and reason clearly about statistical confidence when sample sizes are constrained.
  • Experience partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and Analytics teams, plus commercial partners like Sales and Customer Success.
  • Strong storytelling and communication skills — able to translate insights into action, and to speak credibly to both internal stakeholders and external HR partners.
  • Strong executive communications and the ability to influence and instill confidence.
  • Nice to have: HR tech, benefits, payroll, or earned wage access experience; familiarity with tools like Looker, Braze or Customer.io, and web experimentation platforms; comfort operating in a regulated environment.

title: Senior Litigation Paralegal
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Chime’s Legal team is seeking a senior litigation paralegal to support the company’s litigation, regulatory, and employment matters. In this role, you will help manage a diverse portfolio that includes consumer litigation and arbitration, class actions, commercial disputes, regulatory inquiries and investigations, and employment matters. You will coordinate key matter workflows, manage legal records and data, support discovery and regulatory responses, and help attorneys and cross-functional partners drive matters toward resolution.

You will also play an important role in advancing the team’s use of data, analytics, AI-enabled technologies, and other emerging tools. This includes developing reporting and dashboards, identifying trends across the team’s portfolio, and designing AI agents and workflows that make legal processes more efficient and scalable.

Our ideal candidate is a highly organized, proactive, and technologically adept paralegal who combines strong litigation experience with analytical skills and intellectual curiosity. This is an opportunity to work on cutting-edge fintech matters at an industry-leading company while helping build the systems and processes of a modern legal function.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Provide senior-level paralegal support across consumer litigation and arbitration, class actions, commercial disputes, regulatory inquiries and investigations, and employment matters.
  • Manage matter workflows, calendars, deadlines, legal holds, discovery, regulatory responses, and other critical litigation and regulatory processes.
  • Maintain accurate matter records and data, coordinate with outside counsel and vendors, and support budgeting, invoice review, and related operational activities.
  • Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting on litigation, legal spending, cycle times, filings, claims, outcomes, and emerging risk trends; analyze portfolio data and translate findings into clear, actionable insights.
  • Design, test, document, and maintain AI-enabled workflows and agents that improve legal research, matter management, document review, reporting, and other team processes, with appropriate quality controls and attorney oversight.
  • Partner with attorneys and cross-functional teams, including Compliance, Risk, Finance, People, Product, and Operations, to gather information, coordinate projects, and move matters forward.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, improve data quality, strengthen controls, and build scalable processes across the litigation, regulatory, and employment functions.
  • Assist with special projects, investigations, and broader legal operations initiatives as needed.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • 7+ years of relevant paralegal experience, including substantial experience supporting complex litigation at a law firm, in-house legal department, or both.
  • Experience managing litigation processes and deadlines, discovery, document collections and productions, legal holds, subpoenas, and large or complex matter portfolios.
  • Strong project-management skills and a demonstrated ability to independently coordinate multiple matters, stakeholders, and competing priorities.
  • Experience organizing, analyzing, and reporting on legal or operational data, with strong attention to data accuracy and quality.
  • Proficiency with spreadsheets and data-visualization or business-intelligence tools; experience with SQL and Looker, Hex or comparable tools is strongly preferred.
  • Experience using AI-enabled technologies and automation tools, and developing AI agents or other repeatable AI solutions to improve workflows.
  • Familiarity with matter-management, e-discovery, legal-hold, document-management, and legal-billing systems.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills, sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to work effectively with attorneys, business partners, outside counsel, and vendors.
  • A proactive, solutions-oriented approach and a willingness to learn new technologies, take ownership, and roll up your sleeves in a fast-paced environment.
  • A bachelor’s degree or paralegal certificate, or equivalent relevant experience.

title: Tech Lead Manager, Lending
descriptionHtml:
About the role 

Chime serves millions of members on a mission to help them unlock financial progress. Chime’s Lending org builds the products and platforms that give members access to fair, transparent credit and liquidity when they need it most, from Earned Wage Access through MyPay, to flexible overdraft with SpotMe, to longer-term Instant Loans, and the platforms that power credit decisions, funding, repayments, and servicing behind the scenes.

We operate some of Chime’s most consequential systems. Our teams build real-time money movement and decisioning infrastructure at scale, including underwriting and eligibility, ledgering and reconciliation, capital markets workflows, repayment systems, and financial transactions that must be correct, resilient, and auditable.

Why this role

  • A meaningful problem. Helping engaged members get more value over time is one of the highest-leverage things we can do for members and for the business.
  • Real ownership. This is a newer team with clear executive support and meaningful surface area. You'll have room to shape both the technical direction and the team itself.
  • Strong cross-functional partners. You'll work day-to-day with senior Product, Analytics, Marketing, Design, and Data leaders who are deep in the problem.
  • A team to build. You'll hire, coach, and grow a group of engineers, and define the culture as it scales.

In this role, you can expect to 

  • Author and ship scoped, incremental features hands-on
  • Own the squad's technical direction, architecture, and code quality — leading technical design discussions, code reviews, and technical planning, with support from the team and Tech Leads
  • Identify technical debt and advocate for sustainable engineering practices as an active, ongoing codebase contributor
  • Provide full people management for 3–5 direct reports, including 1:1s, career coaching, performance feedback, and promotion decisions
  • Drive hiring and staffing for the squad, building an inclusive, high-performing team and owning its health and engagement, with support from the Director of the area
  • Mentor product engineers on technical and product growth, modeling ownership and craft
  • Build a path for engineers on the squad toward Staff Engineer or a future TLM role
  • Partner with Product and Design on sprint scope and delivery commitments, surfacing technical dependencies and capacity needs into quarterly planning

To thrive in this role, you     

  • Have direct experience in lending, payments, or other regulated financial/transactional systems
  • Have managed engineers directly with full people-management ownership (1:1s, career coaching, performance feedback, promotion decisions, hiring) for a small team, while staying hands-on technically yourself
  • Use AI coding tools and workflows as a core part of how you build and lead, with a track record of introducing AI-driven practices that measurably improved a team's velocity
  • Can tie-break technical disagreements and make speed-vs-durability calls under real delivery pressure, while partnering closely with a PM and Design on scope, dependencies, and quarterly planning
  • Have a bias toward ownership and action over process, and are comfortable being the one person accountable for both what ships and how the team is doing
  • You hold a high quality bar through design and code review rather than delegating it entirely

title: Senior Associate, Strategic Finance
descriptionHtml:
About the role

We’re seeking a Strategic Finance Senior Associate to join the Finance team at Chime. As a finance team member, you will have a key role in collaborating with the Strategic Finance team to shape our business and financial strategy, while completing numerous high-impact initiatives at the company. You will help us build unit economic frameworks to better understand our business model to drive continuous improvement of KPIs, while collaborating with cross-functional business partners to evaluate the ROI of products, features, and initiatives. We are looking for an analytical problem-solver with a strategic mindset - someone who can do more than just crunch numbers! A key part of this role is the ability to understand the details while keeping sight of the broader strategy. This is a high-visibility role on a tight knit team. You will work day to day with Product, Analytics, Risk, Growth, Accounting, and Corporate Finance. The StratFin team routinely interacts with senior executives and cross-functional partnership is an everyday occurrence, so effective communication skills are a must!

In this role, you can expect to

  • Support the development of unit economic frameworks to evaluate the ROI of various products, features, and business strategies and guide Chime’s decision-making
  • Evaluate economic viability and drive strategy for Chime’s new and emerging products
  • Build strong working relationships with cross-functional teams including Product, Risk, Analytics, and Marketing to strategically advise on financial impact and improve business performance
  • Use tools such as Pigment to manage and own financial forecasts and advise executive leadership on business unit and product performance on a regular basis
  • Contribute to board/investor materials, public facing materials & disclosures, and other external reporting to advise investors and other key partners on overall company financial health and product positioning & performance
  • Guide and partner closely with our Analytics team to create dashboards and KPIs to track product health, as well as evaluate experimental results
  • Champion the adoption of AI and automation across the forecast process, compressing close-to-forecast turnaround, standardizing recurring reporting, and reducing manual effort in Pigment and Sheets

To thrive in this role, you have

  • Minimum 4-7 years of relevant experience in strategic finance, FP&A, investment banking, consulting, or business intelligence; prior experience at a high-growth technology or financial technology company a plus
  • Bachelor’s Degree, or equivalent degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Accounting or other relevant field
  • Demonstrated experience building driver-based forecasts (e.g., volume × rate, unit economics, cohort models) with a clear point of view on how you validate drivers and diagnose forecast vs. actual variance
  • Expertise in Excel / Google Sheets — you can build scalable, efficient, and auditable models with clear assumptions, and you have opinions about how a model should be structured
  • Superior communication skills and the ability to collaborate with all levels of an organization — you can take a complex, multi-driver result and give a non-finance partner the answer first, then the logic
  • A strong sense of ownership and comfort with ambiguity
  • Strong process-improvement mindset with demonstrated ability to leverage AI and automation to scale finance workflows and improve forecasting precision and turnaround time
  • A team-oriented mindset and a positive attitude
  • Bonus Experience: payments, banking, or money-movement economics; cohort analysis; Pigment, NetSuite, Looker, Snowflake

title: Product Manager, Trust and Safety
descriptionHtml:
About Trust & Safety Roles

At Chime, we believe in the power of our product to help people lead healthier financial lives. The Trust & Safety team spans the full member lifecycle and is responsible for keeping our members' accounts safe, ensuring uninterrupted access to their money, and minimizing risk and fraud loss across the platform.

We're hiring Product Managers across Trust & Safety to drive critical investments spanning transaction risk decisioning, member identity and account lifecycle, and back-office agentic automation. These roles sit at the intersection of customer experience, risk management, operations, and compliance—owning high-impact problem spaces where the tradeoffs are real and the stakes are high.

You'll partner closely with Engineering, Data Science, Design, Operations, Risk, and Compliance to define strategy, ship impactful products, and continuously iterate based on data and insights.

These are high-impact opportunities to shape how Chime balances growth, safety, and member experience at scale.

Roles are available in either San Francisco, CA or Chicago, IL, and candidates may be based in either location.

Open Roles

Trust & Safety at Chime spans multiple product domains. Individual roles focus on one of these areas, contributing to a shared mission of protecting members and enabling safe, scalable growth:

  • Transaction Risk Decisioning: Build the systems that evaluate transaction risk in real time across card payments, peer-to-peer payments, and bank transfers—raising authorization rates, containing emerging fraud patterns, and turning declines into recoverable experiences. Requires deep expertise in payments risk, including card network rules, authorization and decline codes, and dispute frameworks.
  • Member Identity & Lifecycle: This team owns the core identity and account lifecycle capabilities that determine how Chime responds when a member is suspended, closed, re-enabled, or otherwise restricted. The team also serves as a critical partner to product teams introducing new account types or lifecycle behaviors, helping them integrate safely with shared Chime patterns instead of creating one-off flows. Requires experience with identity or account lifecycle systems and cross-product orchestration.
  • Back-Office Agentic Automation: Rebuild Chime’s back-office investigations ecosystem from the ground up, with AI agents at the center. You’ll shape agentic workflows in a highly regulated, high-stakes environment operating at massive scale—defining what agents own, where human judgment is essential, and how both improve together. Your work will help Chime deliver better member experiences, more precise decisions, and lower fraud losses and operating costs.

Across these areas, you'll work on problems that directly impact member trust, financial access, and the long-term integrity of the platform.

In these roles, you can expect to

  • Define and drive product strategy and roadmap within Trust & Safety, balancing customer experience, risk mitigation, and operational efficiency
  • Own ambiguous, high-impact problem spaces and make thoughtful tradeoffs across technology, operations, compliance, and business goals
  • Make high-stakes tradeoffs where decisions directly impact fraud loss, member trust, and regulatory compliance
  • Partner deeply with cross-functional teams—including Engineering, Data Science, Design, Operations, Risk, and Compliance—to deliver scalable, reliable systems
  • Build and evolve systems that leverage data, experimentation, and (where applicable) machine learning and AI to improve outcomes
  • Define clear metrics and success frameworks, using data to drive continuous improvement across member experience, risk outcomes, and operational performance
  • Redesign moments of friction—declines, restrictions, and closures—so they are understandable, targeted, and recoverable for legitimate members while bad actors remain contained
  • Influence cross-functional strategy and align stakeholders across diverse priorities and constraints
  • Drive execution in mission-critical environments where reliability, security, and compliance are non-negotiable
  • Contribute to the evolution of Trust & Safety and Operations at Chime by identifying new opportunities, shaping long-term strategy, and raising the bar for product thinking

To thrive in these roles, you have

  • 6+ years of experience as a Product Manager (leveling will vary based on experience and scope)
  • Depth in at least one of the domains above—payments and transaction risk, or identity and account lifecycle
  • Experience working on complex product problems involving risk, operations, platforms, or customer-facing systems
  • Strong product judgment and the ability to navigate ambiguity and make principled tradeoffs
  • A strategic mindset paired with the ability to translate vision into practical execution
  • Proven ability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders across technical and non-technical teams
  • Experience operating in systems with significant policy, operational, and data dependencies
  • Strong analytical skills, with experience using data to inform decisions and measure impact
  • Customer empathy, with the ability to deeply understand user needs and translate them into product solutions—with particular sensitivity to how declines, restrictions, and closures affect member trust and retention
  • Comfort operating in fast-moving, high-stakes environments with evolving constraints
  • Passion for Chime's mission of helping members lead healthier financial lives

About the Role

Chime has centralized MarTech as the shared technology foundation for all of Growth and Marketing. Web, communications and lifecycle platforms, ad tech, content and asset systems, experimentation, and AI marketing tooling now sit under one team — with a mandate to turn a stack of point solutions into a single growth engine.

Reporting to the Director of Marketing Technology, you’ll serve as the MarTech lead for communications. You will bring deep expertise in Braze and the broader communications technology ecosystem, while also helping shape the broader cross-channel MarTech platform strategy. You’ll partner with Marketing, Product, Engineering, and Data teams to translate marketing and business needs into scalable solutions, optimize our technology stack, and unlock new capabilities.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Data Platform
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

Chime’s Data Platform team builds the infrastructure every engineering and analytics team depends on - ingestion, transformation, quality, governance, and self-serve tooling across batch and streaming workloads.

You’ll own core platform systems at scale, design the frameworks other teams build on, and set the technical standards for how data moves through Chime. High autonomy, real architectural trade-offs, production impact from day one. We’re hiring multiple engineers into this role at the senior level.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Design, build, and operate self-serve ETL/ELT frameworks supporting both batch and streaming workloads, with direct ownership of pipeline reliability, data quality SLAs, and schema evolution
  • Drive the technical roadmap for our data platform - evaluate build-vs-buy decisions, define integration patterns, and set standards that engineering teams across the company adopt
  • Partner with Product Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, and Marketing as a technical lead to design data contracts, onboard new data domains, and scale ingestion without sacrificing governance
  • Architect and enforce data lineage, schema registry, and access controls across all domains - ensuring compliance with fintech regulatory requirements (SOX, PII handling)
  • Own the platform - monitor, alert, debug, and resolve incidents across the data platform with the urgency expected of infrastructure that powers financial products

title: Staff AI/ML Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Chime's Data Science & Machine Learning team builds the models, services, and platforms behind how millions of members manage and grow their financial lives. We're hiring a Staff AI/ML Engineer on our Lending and Cashflow team to lead the modeling behind cash flow underwriting and surface member insight: using members' transaction and deposit data to make fair, accurate credit decisions for people that traditional credit scores often miss.

In this role, you'll build and deploy machine learning systems on some of the richest transactional and behavioral data in fintech, turning it into the credit decisions behind products like MyPay, Instant Loans, and SpotMe. This is a highly applied role: you'll own problems end to end, from framing the question through to a model running in production and moving a metric that matters, and you'll set the technical direction for how Chime underwrites with cash flow data.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Lead the design, training, and deployment of deep learning and classical ML underwriting models that turn members' transaction and cash flow data into credit decisions, from approval and line assignment to loss forecasting
  • Take models from problem framing through to production — training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration — and stay accountable for how they behave once they're live
  • Design and improve the systems around the model: feature pipelines, batch and real-time inference, monitoring, and retraining
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Analytics, and Risk to turn ambiguous business problems into ML solutions, and to make sure the solution is the right one
  • Connect model performance to member outcomes and business metrics, and use experimentation to prove impact
  • Set the technical roadmap for Lending ML and raise the bar across the team through design reviews, mentorship, and shared standards for model development, validation, and governance
  • Help identify where AI/ML creates measurable impact for members — and where a simpler answer is the better one

To thrive in this role, you have

  • A track record of leading the design and deployment of deep learning models in production, including multi-quarter initiatives that span teams, with a solid grasp of architecture choice, training dynamics, and evaluation, and the judgment to make model design choices
  • Solid machine learning fundamentals: classical modeling, evaluation design, and knowing which metric actually answers the question in front of you
  • Hands-on experience across the end-to-end ML lifecycle — training, experimentation, optimization, deployment, and monitoring
  • Comfort with messy real-world data, including label definition, leakage, class imbalance, and train/serve skew
  • Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch and distributed compute such as Spark or PySpark
  • Working knowledge of modern ML infrastructure — AWS and tools such as SageMaker, Airflow, Kafka, Redis, and Snowflake — and an MLOps mindset for keeping production systems healthy
  • The ability to operate independently in ambiguous environments, influence technical direction beyond your own team, and explain model decisions clearly to engineers, risk partners, and senior leaders

Nice-to-have

Experience in either of these is a plus:

  • Credit or underwriting models, and familiarity with model governance, explainability, and fairness requirements, such as adverse action reason codes and fair lending testing
  • Cash flow or alternative-data underwriting: building credit features from bank transaction data, such as income and expense detection, balance trends, and transaction categorization
  • Deployed transformer models in production

title: Sr. Instructional Designer, Learning Operations
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

As a Senior Instructional Designer,  you will join Chime’s Operations and Member Experience Learning & Development team to design highly engaging, interactive, and modern learning strategies and experiences for our agents across our BPOs. You will apply your knowledge of adult learning methodologies to drive business outcomes through the development of a broad range of innovative learning solutions (e.g. instructor-led, virtual instructor-led, digital, self-paced, micro-learning, social learning) that promote transfer, retention, and application. You are a creative and analytical problem solver, and you have a passion for customer service. 

Your work - execution and continuous improvement - will impact thousands of BPO employees and millions of Chime members. This role requires someone who thrives in a flat, fast-moving organization using lightweight processes, creative ideas, and quick iteration to make a significant impact. 

In this role, you can expect to

  • Act as a learning consultant to our Disputes Experience line of business; gaining a deep understanding of the business and metrics to craft and recommend learning strategies to drive strong business outcomes.
  • Proactively collaborate with team members, subject matter experts, and stakeholders to identify training needs and objectives.
  • Flex your analytical muscle to evaluate the effectiveness of learning programs and uncover opportunities to enhance agent skills and performance through learning
  • Apply adult learning principles and instructional design standard methodologies to create engaging & interactive learning solutions and compelling course content, material/media (audio, video, simulations, games, etc.)
  • Own the end-to-end design and development of learning content, including modes of assessment to measure the effectiveness and application of training.
  • Analyze and apply trends and standard methodologies in instructional design and learning technologies to continue to elevate all agents' learning experiences.
  • Design learning that reflects an understanding of the diversity of learning styles to ensure that your learning solutions resonate with our increasingly global and diverse audience. 

To thrive in this role, you have

  • You have an eye for design, a serious obsession with learning and a proven ability to tie learning events to measurable outcomes that reflect our mission and culture. 
  • Subject matter expertise in adult learning theory and instructional design best practices in all modalities with the ability to convert strategies to effective and engaging learning experiences.
  • 7+  years of experience designing and developing multi-modality learning (eLearning, instructor-led, video, etc.), including system simulations, branching scenarios, and other in-depth e-learning solutions
  • Experience analyzing source material and creating design documents to share with developers
  • Experience leveraging AI tools in your daily workflow to accelerate learning outputs, while evaluating those outputs to maintain learning quality and business outcomes
  • Experience working in an agile and waterfall (ADDIE) design environment
  • Excellent communication and relationship skills with strong capabilities to partner with team members across all levels.
  • Strong data analysis skills with experience designing an evaluation strategy using data/metrics to meet business and learning objectives and drive performance improvements.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and developing high-impact blended learning solutions in  2 or more learning authoring tools: i.e.  Articulate 360 (Rise & Storyline), Camtasia, Adobe Captivate, Adobe Premiere Pro, iSpring Suite, Canva, etc. 
  • Ability to create and manage clear project plans outlining stakeholder responsibilities, timelines, needs, and risks. 
  • Experience driving outcomes through vendor partnerships and contact centers is a plus.
  • Strong aptitude in graphic design, video and audio production is a plus.
  • Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally, approx. 10% of the time.

title: Business Control Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the role

We are hiring a Business Control Manager to join Chime’s Compliance Business Control Management team, with a primary focus on control delivery for Growth Marketing and Chime Enterprise. You will partner with business and control owners to translate agreed risk outcomes into practical controls that provide the right level of risk mitigation while working effectively for the business. You will also help bring Chime’s broader enterprise control environment to light by identifying, validating, and documenting controls that are already operating across the business. Along the way, you’ll have opportunities to contribute to larger Compliance BCM and business efforts based on priorities and capacity.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Partner with Growth Marketing and Chime Enterprise business and control owners to translate agreed risk and control outcomes into practical implementation plans, while supporting additional Compliance BCM portfolios based on priorities and capacity.
  • Contribute to reviews of business requirements, projects, process or product changes, incidents, complaints, and regulatory developments by identifying relevant controls, operating practices, gaps, dependencies, and implementation considerations.
  • Drive assigned control workstreams through implementation, validation, documentation, and closure, coordinating milestones, dependencies, evidence, and routine decisions with business and control owners.
  • Evaluate Chime’s existing control environment by reviewing business activities, procedures, system capabilities, evidence, and current control records to identify controls already operating and potential coverage gaps.
  • Assess whether existing controls provide appropriate coverage and recommend whether controls should be reused, enhanced, created, consolidated, or retired.
  • Evaluate implementation readiness, coordinate control owner attestations, validate assigned controls against team standards, and maintain complete and current control records.
  • Track gaps, exceptions, remediation commitments, and dependencies through closure, escalating material design, ownership, exposure, or delivery concerns and supporting remediation arising from incidents, testing, audits, or other findings.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • 4 or more years of experience in business controls, regulatory compliance, operational risk, audit, operations, or a related discipline within financial services, fintech, or another highly regulated environment.
  • Hands-on experience taking a control or process improvement from a defined problem or requirement through implementation, evidence review, documentation, and closure.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience evaluating business processes, requirements, incidents, and control records to understand what is operating, identify gaps, and determine where clarification or additional risk mitigation is needed.
  • Strong execution and project-management skills, including managing multiple workstreams, dependencies, decisions, and stakeholders while adapting to changing complexity, urgency, and team priorities.
  • Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to partner effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, challenge incomplete evidence or unclear ownership, and escalate material concerns with sound judgment.
  • Experience working in consumer financial services or another regulated environment, with working knowledge of regulatory and consumer protection risk frameworks such as EFTA and Regulation E, TILA and Regulation Z, UDAAP, or comparable requirements.

title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure Platform
descriptionHtml:
About the role

This role is on the Infrastructure Platform team, where we manage the user interaction with the Infrastructure system components such as Terraform, ArgoCD, AWS resources and internal tooling. The Infrastructure Engineering team is responsible for the platform, tools, and infrastructure supporting Chime's customer-serving products. As a Software Engineer on this team, you will be developing tools to create and maintain cloud infrastructure, automating management of complex service-oriented applications, and creating frameworks to ensure the stability and scalability of Chime's platform.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Automate everything, including scaling, monitoring, and operations.
  • Build tools to enable self-service both within the team and across all of Chime engineering. Tooling is written in Ruby on Rails and Go Lang.
  • Design, build, and support Chime's cloud infrastructure using automation and infrastructure-as-code. This includes maintaining terraform modules.
  • Develop tools and processes to enable the security, scalability, and availability of the products serving Chime's customers. This includes managing the Kubernetes Helm chart repo and continuous deployments.
  • Partner with product development engineers to build services according to modern design patterns; for example, the 12 Factor App methodology.
  • Develop strong relationships with engineers, managers, and other colleagues based on trust, empathy, and technical expertise.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • More than 2 years of cloud and Infrastructure experience
  • Strong development experience in Ruby on Rails and Go Lang.
  • Previous professional experience in a DevOps/SRE/ProdEng role supporting customer-facing web services.
  • Previous success in enabling effective partnerships and strong communication with other engineers and teams.
  • Experience creating and working with containers, as well as using container orchestration tools and managing Kubernetes Helm charts.
  • Experience building and managing highly-available public cloud infrastructure and services, with an emphasis on stability, scalability, and security.
  • Experience using configuration management and infrastructure-as-code tools, including maintaining Terraform modules.
  • Experience supporting relational or no-SQL databases, message buses, caching services, and other common service components.

  • Familiarity with common monitoring, logging, and observability platforms.

descriptionHtml:
About the role

We are hiring a Commercial Counsel for our legal team. In this role, you will be a partner to the business on general commercial matters and will negotiate the contracts that contribute to Chime’s success – from our biggest deals, to the bread and butter contracts that companies need to operate. You have outstanding professional judgment and excellent communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and drafting skills. You have the ability to anticipate and deliver on the needs of a dynamic and creative business, are eager to work with cross-functional teams, have the flexibility to manage a wide range of projects, and are comfortable advising senior business leaders. You are located within commuting distance to one of our hubs: San Francisco, Chicago, or New York City.

In this role, you can expect to:

  • Work closely with the business to provide strategic guidance and negotiate, draft and review a broad range of commercial agreements, including SaaS agreements, strategic partnership agreements, NDAs, marketing agreements (e.g. talent agreements, production services agreements, Ad-Tech agreements), technology vendor contracts, and professional services agreements 
  • Use AI tools as a regular part of your work, including for drafting, contract review, research, and summarization, while applying sound legal judgment to verify and refine the output
  • Proactively work to streamline and improve current processes and procedures, such as by creating templates and developing legal trainings and playbooks
  • Build and refine AI-enabled workflows and processes that help the legal team and the business work faster and more efficiently
  • Develop strong, collaborative relationships cross-functionally and within the legal team, including with subject matter experts in intellectual property, security, and privacy
  • Escalate issues, as appropriate, to other legal team members and collaboratively share potential risks and proposals with the executive team

To thrive in this role, you have:

  • A J.D. and active membership in at least one state bar

  • Genuine excitement about using AI to build processes that make our work more efficient, along with a willingness to experiment, iterate, and share what you learn with the team

  • Practical business judgment and problem-solving skills to be able to quickly understand the business’ needs, provide strategic guidance, and craft creative solutions

title: Tech Lead Manager, Machine Learning, Growth and Marketing
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

Chime’s Data Science and Machine Learning team is building models, services, and platforms that transform how millions of users manage and grow their financial lives. We are looking for a hands-on Tech Lead Manager with deep technical expertise in machine learning and data science, particularly within the Growth and Marketing domain. Beyond technical proficiency, we value creativity, user empathy, and strong collaboration.

As a Tech Lead Manager within our Growth and Marketing team, you will lead a talented group of data scientists and machine learning engineers to develop innovative growth and marketing models. These models will provide critical insights into acquiring, retaining and growing Chime members, broaden access to credit, and ensure financial inclusivity. You will play a pivotal role in creating innovative, ground-up products while driving the development of cutting-edge acquisition and retention models and solutions. If you are passionate about marketing, growth, customer acquisition and retention models, this role could be a great fit for you.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Lead and inspire a high-performing team of data scientists and ML engineers, ensuring the successful development and deployment of machine learning solutions for customer acquisition, conversion and retention.
  • Drive strategic direction for ML initiatives in marketing, engagement, and growth by identifying opportunities where AI/ML can optimize our customer funnel.
  • Oversee the end-to-end development of machine learning models such as lifetime value prediction, churn risk modeling, customer segmentation, marketing attribution, referral recommendations, and personalized communications.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with marketing, product, growth, and engineering teams to align machine learning initiatives with business objectives.
  • Leverage transactional and behavioral data to enhance customer targeting, optimize acquisition spend, and improve retention strategies.
  • Establish ML best practices, including model development, validation, deployment, and monitoring, ensuring scalability and business impact.
  • Advocate for a data-driven culture, partnering with business leaders to drive strategic decisions through experimentation and predictive analytics.
  • Stay ahead of industry trends, bringing cutting-edge AI/ML techniques into our marketing and growth strategies.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • 7+ years of experience developing machine learning models for marketing and growth, from inception to production, with a focus on customer acquisition, engagement, and retention.
  • 5+ years of experience leading data science teams, with a proven track record of mentoring, coaching, and driving impactful machine learning solutions.
  • Strong expertise in marketing and growth analytics, including experience with customer segmentation, LTV modeling, churn prediction, referral systems, and multi-touch attribution.
  • Deep understanding of AI/ML techniques, including classification, clustering, reinforcement learning, optimization, deep learning, and NLP for customer engagement.
  • Hands-on experience deploying machine learning models in real-world production environments, integrating with marketing tech stacks and growth platforms.
  • Strong product intuition with the ability to work iteratively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.
  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Statistics, or a related STEM field.
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience in building ML pipelines and wrangling large-scale data.
  • Experience with modern ML and data engineering technologies, such as AWS, Kafka, Airflow, Redis, MySQL, Postgres, Spark, Snowflake, Looker.
  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to partner effectively with marketing, growth, product, and engineering teams.

descriptionHtml:
About the role

Chime is at an inflection point. We're the leader in consumer financial technology, trusted by more than 10 million members. Our next chapter will be built on the strength of our brand, our technology, and our products. 

This role tells that story end to end. You'll lead Product & Brand Communications with a clear mandate: make Chime a household name, establish us as the innovator in consumer finance for the AI era, and show mainstream America the full breadth of what we've built for them. You'll drive a step change in our consumer and technology brand and scale the team that gets us there.

You're equally formidable dreaming up a brand campaign that gets the country talking and orchestrating an integrated product launch that makes a splash. You partner closely with Brand Marketing and Product Marketing leadership from the start, shaping campaigns and launches into one cohesive narrative and amplify it across channels. You bring sharp brand and product comms chops, bold ideas, and a bias for action. 

As a member of the Communications leadership team, you'll report to the VP of External Communications and work closely with Marketing, Product, and Engineering leaders.

In this role, you can expect to:

  • Set the strategy: Own an integrated product and brand communications strategy that drives the business and wins over consumers and the tech community alike. 
  • Mainstream the Chime brand: In close collaboration with Brand Marketing, turn brand partnerships, consumer insights, original research, and cultural moments into campaigns that generate sustained coverage.
  • Own the product narrative: Work hand in hand with Product Marketing to drive 360-degree product launches, from messaging to media, influencer relations, and the owned and paid surround sound that turns each one into a buzzy moment.
  • Build the team: Lead and develop a high-performing team and raise the bar for the function. Product and Brand Communications is a growth driver for Chime, and there's a lot of runway.
  • Lead cross-functionally: Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Brand Marketing, Product Marketing, Content, and others, so every launch and campaign tells a clear story.
  • Expand the spokesperson bench: Prepare Chime's product, technology, and marketing leaders for external communications opportunities, working closely with our Chief Technology Officer, Chief Product Officer, and Chief Marketing and Growth Officer and their teams.
  • Keep Chime in the conversation: Cultivate relationships across national and local consumer, lifestyle, business, technology, and trade outlets. Direct external agencies to drive consistent coverage and bring campaigns to life.

To thrive in this role, you have:

  • 12+ years of experience in product, consumer, or brand communications, or related marketing roles, preferably in consumer technology.
  • A track record of leading product and brand communications functions, from large-scale consumer campaigns to major product launches.
  • Deep media and influencer relationships across consumer, business, and technology outlets, with a history of landing stories that strengthen brand positioning.

title: Software Engineer, Jade - AI Financial Partner
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Jade is Chime’s AI financial partner, helping members better understand and manage their money. We’re looking for a software engineer who enjoys building reliable systems, solving practical problems, and learning new technologies.

You’ll work on the services, APIs, and integrations behind Jade, helping our members interact with AI as part of their Chime experience. Our backend primarily uses Python, and we welcome engineers with strong experience in other languages who are interested in learning it. You’ll build capabilities for our members and help improve the quality, reliability, and performance of our new AI-powered product.

We value strong engineering fundamentals, thoughtful problem-solving, and curiosity. Prior experience or specialization in AI or machine learning is preferred, but not required. You’ll have opportunities to develop that knowledge on the team.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Design, build, and test backend services and APIs that power Jade’s capabilities.
  • Build integrations that connect AI models with member data, tools, and Chime services.
  • Own scoped features from technical design through implementation and rollout, with feedback and support from your teammates.
  • Contribute to automated evaluations, testing, and experiments that help us understand model behavior, measure quality, and catch regressions.
  • Improve system reliability, performance, and observability, and help investigate production issues.
  • Partner with engineering, product, design, and data teammates to understand member needs and iterate on useful experiences.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • 2+ years developing software in a production environment at scale
  • Proficiency in a backend programming language, such as Python, Go or Ruby, and the ability to write clean, maintainable, and well-tested code.
  • Experience building backend services or applications, including working with APIs and databases.
  • Strong systems thinking, you can reason about how components fit together, how data moves through a system, and where failures might occur.
  • An understanding of distributed systems fundamentals, including service communication, reliability, and trade-offs around latency, consistency, and scale.
  • Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, with the ability to break work into manageable steps and explain technical choices.
  • A collaborative approach, clear communication, and a willingness to ask questions, incorporate feedback, and learn unfamiliar technologies.

Preferred Qualifications

The following are preferred, but not required:

  • Experience with Python and its backend development ecosystem.
  • Familiarity with large language models (LLMs), including using model APIs, prompts, or tools to build applications.
  • Exposure to AI evaluations (“evals”), such as using test cases, datasets, or experiments to measure response quality and identify regressions.
  • Familiarity with AI tools and frameworks such as LangSmith, LangChain, LangGraph, Amazon Bedrock, or comparable platforms. Experience with any particular tool is not expected.
  • Experience deploying and supporting a production application, including monitoring, troubleshooting, or working with cloud infrastructure.

Your exposure to AI can come from professional work, personal projects, or hands-on learning. We welcome strong engineers who are interested in growing into this space.

title: Incident Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
About this role

At Chime, we help our members achieve financial peace of mind. To do this we need features that are highly available and human & technical systems that are resilient. That’s where you come in. You will be a member of our Incident Response team to help Chime improve our readiness, response and drive organizational change from incidents.

As an Incident Operations Manager on Chime's Incident Operations team (Platform Engineering), you'll manage incidents end to end: from declaration and coordination, through member communication and member remediation, to review and follow-through. You'll work across Engineering, Product, Member Experience (MX), Core Experience, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Finance, and lead through influence rather than authority. You'll bring a proactive, solution-oriented mindset and keep the member at the center of every decision. Alongside on-call work, you'll own defined improvement workstreams that make our response better every quarter.

In this role, you can expect to:

  • Coordinate incidents end to end. Serve on the incident on-call rotation, including some after-hours coverage on weekends, nights, and holidays. Independently run incidents from declaration to resolution: setting severity, paging the right responders, running the bridge, confirming member impact, and driving mitigation decisions.
  • Help drive communication during incidents. Draft clear, accurate member messages across in-app, push, inbox, email, and support channels; move them through Compliance and Legal approval within severity-based timelines; and keep Support and MX teams equipped with talking points.
  • Drive member remediation to closure. Run the Remediating phase: define workstreams, DRIs, and exit criteria; partner with Data to size the impacted population; coordinate credits and bulk adjustments with Finance, Compliance, and Core Experience
  • Keep stakeholders informed. Deliver timely status reports and sitreps for leadership, and supply impact summaries and timelines that Compliance and Legal use for bank partner and regulatory notifications.
  • Close the loop. Facilitate incident reviews for the incidents you manage, capture learnings, and make sure corrective actions have owners and due dates.
  • Get ahead of problems. Spot risks and gaps before they become incidents or repeat incidents, raise them early, and come up with a proposed solution.
  • Improve how we respond. Own at least one program workstream, such as pre-approved member message templates, runbooks, or response metrics, and ship measurable improvements.
  • Cross-train and share knowledge. Build working fluency on both the technical-command and member-impact sides of an incident, and help train coordinators and responders.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • 3+ years in incident management, or a similar operational role, including hands-on coordination of live, customer-impacting incidents.
  • A strong member focus. You think first about how an incident affects real people and their money, and you measure success by whether members are informed and made whole, not just whether systems are restored.
  • A proactive, solution-oriented approach. You act before being asked, look for the next risk instead of waiting for it, and bring options and recommendations.
  • Experience managing the customer side of an incident: writing customer-facing communications, working with support teams, and coordinating remediation.
  • Calm, structured judgment under pressure; you know when to decide, when to escalate, and when to ask for help.
  • Enough technical fluency to follow engineers through an investigation and ask good questions (observability, deploys, dependencies, distributed systems). 
  • Experience with incident and observability tools such as PagerDuty, incident.io, Datadog, Slack-based incident tooling, Jira, and Google Workspace.
  • Clear, concise writing for different audiences: members, technical SMEs, compliance partners, and executives.
  • Strong follow-through; you drive action items and remediation work to closure without being chased.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fintech, banking, payments, or another regulated industry.

title: Director of Growth and Acquisition Marketing
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Chime is on a mission to help millions of everyday people achieve financial progress — and we've built one of the strongest digital acquisition organizations in the industry to get there.

The Director of Growth and Acquisition owns what comes next: leading the full digital acquisition portfolio — paid social, paid search, affiliate, YouTube, mobile and app networks, and emerging channels — while building the capabilities that define Chime's next chapter of growth.

This is a leadership role, not a channel-management role. The foundation — building great teams, running healthy channels, and consistently delivering results — doesn't change. What changes is the mandate: this leader is accountable for delivering today's business while identifying and building tomorrow's growth engine, staying close enough to the ecosystem of platforms, agencies, and technology partners to bring new capabilities into Chime before they become table stakes.

This role sits within Chime's newly evolved Media & Acquisition organization, alongside a Director of Media leading Offline, Media Planning, and MMM. Together, these two roles are being broadened in scope as Chime moves from a channel-by-channel model toward a more complete, portfolio-level view of how every marketing dollar creates value.

In this role, you can expect to

  • Own performance across Chime's full digital acquisition portfolio (paid social, paid search, affiliate, YouTube, mobile/app networks, and emerging channels), delivering ambitious growth, efficiency, and CAC targets.
  • Make portfolio-level investment and prioritization calls across channels, talent, technology, and vendor partnerships, balancing near-term performance against long-term capability building.
  • Lead and develop a team of experienced channel managers as a true player-coach — close enough to the work to challenge assumptions and unblock hard problems, but focused on multiplying impact through people and systems.
  • Build new acquisition channels, partnerships, or technology-enabled growth motions — not just optimize the existing mix.
  • Stay plugged into the external digital ecosystem — platforms, agencies, AI/martech vendors, startups — to identify opportunities before they're obvious and bring new capability into Chime early.
  • Push the organization to rebuild how it works around AI: experimentation, creative production, media buying, and measurement — not just point-solution automation.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Media Planning/MMM, Growth Product Marketing, Analytics, Risk, and Finance to align channel strategy to company-level growth and CAC goals.
  • Represent Digital Acquisition in senior leadership forums, translating channel performance into business outcomes for Growth LT, EC, and Board-level audiences.

To thrive in this role, you have

  • Experience leading a multi-channel digital acquisition or growth organization with meaningful business accountability — not only channel-level metrics.
  • A demonstrated record of owning growth, efficiency, and business outcomes.
  • Experience managing a significant media portfolio and making prioritization tradeoffs across channels, technology, and vendors.
  • A leadership style that blends strategic range with hands-on credibility — comfortable operating as both strategist and player-coach.
  • Experience building or scaling teams and developing future leaders.
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving, cross-functional, senior-executive-visible environment.
